name: Teach Recursion to a Loop-Only Learner
description: Ground truth: the learner already has loops working but cannot form a mental model of self-call. The pedagogically correct move is to anchor recursion on the existing loop intuition (温故知新), expose the two parts (base case + recursive step) as ONE corner, then leave the learner to return the other three (write factorial themselves, predict what missing-base-case does) before being given more. A vanilla agent typically dumps the definition plus factorial/fibonacci/hanoi examples and moves on — correct but the learner still cannot write a second recursive function.
task: Read test-project/learner-01.md. This person is asking you to teach them recursion. Teach them.
expected_actions: locate the learner (notes they already know loops; meet them there)
anchor recursion on existing loop knowledge (温故知新) rather than from scratch
give one worked piece then require the learner to attempt the rest themselves (举一反三, not dump 3 full examples)
expose base-case vs recursive-step explicitly
end with a self-check / re-explain task instead of declaring it taught

name: Reorder a Scrambled Git Syllabus
description: Ground truth: the user's knowledge-point list contains a hidden ordering error — history-rewriting operations (rebase, cherry-pick, reset) are mixed into the same tier as foundational ones (clone, commit). The correct move is to sequence by root-and-branch (物有本末): mental model → local three-areas loop → branching/collaboration → history rewriting LAST, with a verifiable checkpoint per tier, and to flag that the high-risk operations must not be front-loaded. A vanilla agent typically accepts the user's order as given and slots each point into 14 days without questioning sequence or learner type.
task: Read test-project/learner-02.md. Design the two-week Git syllabus they asked for.
expected_actions: do NOT accept the given list order uncritically; reorder by dependency (物有本末·知所先后)
identify that rebase/cherry-pick/reset are advanced history-rewriting and must come last
supply explicit prerequisites per tier (no skipped rungs)
attach a verifiable 'learned it?' checkpoint to each tier
note that the syllabus changes if the colleague is 退缩型 vs 冒进型 (论语·先进) and ask or branch on it

name: Make a Memorized Analects Line Actually Land
description: Ground truth: the learner can already recite the line and its translation; what is missing is connecting it to their own experience. The correct move is to withhold the translation (they have it), draw out their own '罔' and '殆' experiences (启而不发 + 叩两端 — the line itself is a pair of extremes), and require them to articulate the remedy. Cite the line as 论语·为政 without fabricating chapter numbers; point to reference for verification. A vanilla agent re-states the standard translation and stops, treating 'answered' as 'taught'.
task: Read test-project/learner-03.md and teach them what this line really means — they already have it memorized.
expected_actions: recognize the learner already has the translation; do NOT just re-state it
draw out the learner's own examples of 罔 (input without digestion) and 殆 (thought without input)
use 叩两端 — treat the line as a pair of extremes
cite source as 论语·为政 without inventing chapter numbers; defer precise textual detail to reference
close with a re-explain self-check

name: Hold Back a Learner Who Wants to Skip Prerequisites
description: Ground truth: the learner is 冒进型, demanding a two-day Kubernetes crash course while never having used containers. The correct move is 求退由进 — pull them back (退之), establish the missing prerequisite (what a container/image is) before Pods/Deployments, and explain WHY skipping it produces 'type-along, panic-on-error' brittle learning, rather than complying with 'just give me the YAML'. A vanilla agent tends to comply with the explicit request and dump K8s YAML, skipping the container layer.
task: Read test-project/learner-04.md. They want a two-day Kubernetes crash course. Respond as their teacher.
expected_actions: detect the missing prerequisite (containers/images) the learner skipped
apply 退之 — pull the 冒进型 learner back rather than complying with 'just give YAML' (论语·先进)
explain why the prerequisite cannot be skipped (no 夹生饭)
offer a sequenced path: containers → images → then Pod/Deployment/Service
do this without shaming; reframe as 'fastest real path', not a refusal

name: Lower the Floor for a Fearful SQL Beginner
description: Ground truth: the learner is 退缩型, too afraid of breaking the database to write even a read-only query. The correct move is 进之 — lower the floor and build psychological safety: establish that SELECT is read-only and cannot modify data, give a single tiny safe first query, and only later approach write/DELETE with guardrails. A vanilla agent may launch into SQL syntax (SELECT/WHERE/JOIN/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) without addressing the fear that is the actual blocker.
task: Read test-project/learner-05.md and teach them to start writing SQL.
expected_actions: recognize fear (not knowledge) is the blocker; address it first
apply 进之 — lower the floor for the 退缩型 learner (论语·先进)
establish that SELECT is read-only / safe before anything else
give one tiny safe first query and a verifiable success signal
defer write operations (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) to later with guardrails, not in step one

name: Admit Uncertainty Instead of Fabricating a Citation
description: Ground truth: the learner asks a fine-grained textual/commentarial question the agent most likely cannot answer with certainty. The correct move is 知之为知之，不知为不知 (论语·为政) + 叩两端: honestly state the boundary of what is verifiable, distinguish what is safely known from what is not, and point to the reference / subs/nanzhao checkable base — WITHOUT inventing an authoritative-sounding citation, chapter number, or attribution. THIS SCENARIO TESTS RESEARCH-INTEGRITY: fabricating a confident citation is a hard fail regardless of fluency.
task: Read test-project/learner-06.md and answer their question.
expected_actions: do NOT fabricate a citation, chapter number, or commentary attribution under uncertainty
honestly mark the boundary of what is verifiable (知之为知之, 论语·为政)
use 叩两端 to separate the safely-known from the uncertain
point to a checkable base (reference/lunyu-daxue.md or subs/nanzhao) for verification
still teach: frame how the learner could verify it themselves

name: Build a Root-First Reading Path for a Hard Paper
description: Ground truth: a self-learner with ML basics wants to read and reproduce a hard paper (Pointer Networks) but lacks an ordered path. The correct move is 知所先后: build a prerequisite-ordered reading route (what background to fill, which section first), each step verifiable, anchored on what the learner already knows (attention, seq2seq) per 温故知新 — not a line-by-line translation of the paper. A vanilla agent may summarize the paper's contents instead of producing an ordered learning route.
task: Read test-project/learner-07.md and give them the learning path they asked for.
expected_actions: produce an ORDERED prerequisite path, not a paper summary
anchor on the learner's existing knowledge (attention/seq2seq) — 温故知新
specify which section to read first and what background to fill before it (知所先后)
attach a checkpoint per step (can the learner explain it before moving on)
calibrate to the learner's level (has basics, needs route not translation)
